messages:
alice: Heads up — setting up GCP KMS for a new Private deployment. We need guidance on service account binding patterns, keyring location, audit log routing, and the rotation/rewrap path. Any gotchas?
ben: Quick Q — are we doing per-tenant keyrings or a shared keyring in the customer's project? Also: cross-project SA impersonation concerns.
carmen: For Private, our default is to put the keyring in the customer project (owner-managed). Then we request explicit bindings to our control-plane SA for encrypt/decrypt. Per-tenant keyrings are safer for isolation but more admin overhead.
dave: Important: our control plane uses service account impersonation to call KMS in the customer project. That means the customer needs to grant the impersonating SA the KMS role, and also grant our control-plane callers iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken or iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the impersonated SA.
alice: Can you paste a minimal IAM snippet?
carmen: Sure — example (customer applies these):
```
# grant encrypt/decrypt on a specific cryptoKey
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding my-key \
  --location=global --keyring=redwood-keyring \
  --member="serviceAccount:redwood-control@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"

# grant token-creation on the impersonated SA (if we need to impersonate from our infra)
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding impersonated-sa@customer-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member="serviceAccount:redwood-control@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
```
dave: Also note we can scope the KMS binding to the key resource (preferred) rather than the entire project.
ben: Audit logs: make sure Admin Activity and Data Access logs for KMS are enabled and routed to the customer's org sink or SIEM. We need those for rewrap/rotation forensic trails. Example sink: 
```
gcloud logging sinks create kms-sink bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/ops-bq \
  --log-filter='resource.type="cloudkms_crypto_key"'
```
carmen: Rotation/rewrap patterns — important distinctions:
- Primary rotate only: create a new CryptoKeyVersion and make it primary. New encrypts use the new primary. Existing ciphertexts remain encrypted under the old version until rewrap.
- Eager rewrap: our rewrap job decrypts DEKs with the old version and encrypts with the new primary. This requires decrypt permissions on the key (roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter for the SA doing the job).
- Lazy rewrap: decrypt-and-reencrypt happens as objects are written/updated by the application; less immediate cost but slower convergence.

If the customer forbids us from having decrypt rights (customer policy), we can only rotate primary and do lazy rewrap client-side. There's no KMS API to rewrap without decrypting to plaintext unless the customer runs the rewrap inside their environment.
alice: So to support eager rewrap, we must ask the customer to grant our ops SA decrypt rights on the key or run a rewrap job inside their tenant. Noted.
dave: Also watch VPC Service Controls / access boundary: if the customer project is inside a VPC-SC perimeter, straight calls from our control plane will be blocked unless they add our service identity to the perimeter or use a customer-hosted rewrap job.
ben: Key location: region vs global. If the keyring is regional make sure the Private deployment region matches or we add latency + egress considerations.
carmen: Ops policy: avoid granting roles/cloudkms.admin unless needed. Minimal set: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter for runtime encrypt/decrypt; roles/cloudkms.viewer for metadata; roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator only scoped to the impersonated SA resource.
alice: Any compliance notes for retention?
sre-oncall: We need KMS audit logs retained for 400 days per compliance. Also export rewrap, rotate, and setPrimary operations to our SIEM. File a ticket for log-retention config.
ben: One more — we should document rollback: if a rewrap job fails halfway, we need idempotent rewrap with version metadata on each object (store keyVersion used). Then we can resume safely.
carmen: Agreed — store metadata: encrypted-DEK, kms-key-name, kms-key-version. That lets us detect stale ciphertext and rewrap deterministically.
alice: I'll draft a private-deploy KMS checklist: keyring in customer project, explicit key-level bindings, logging sink, rewrap plan (owner-run vs redwood-run), region match, VPC-SC check, and rotation runbook. Will ping legal for cross-project flow approval.
dave: I'll add a proof-of-concept script for eager rewrap (needs decrypt scope). Posting in #eng-infra when ready.
infra-bot: Note added to infra backlog: PROJ-5421 add KMS rotation POC and checklist.
sre-oncall: Thanks — please include a step to verify keyVersion metadata on a sample object before mass rewrap.
ben: I'll circle back with a draft doc and concrete gcloud commands for customers who want to self-host rewrap.
alice: Perfect. Closing thread once doc PR is up. :ok_hand:
